name: forth-cli
title: Forth CLI
blurb: Forth CLI on gforth: byte-exact counting over a memory block, hand-rolled argv parser, a four-word test harness, terminal reads behind one file

verify.name: usage-error
verify.cmd: set +e; ./bin/{{ npm_name }} --bogus >/dev/null 2>&1; status=$?; echo "exit status: $status"; test "$status" -eq 2

verify.name: missing-file
verify.cmd: set +e; ./bin/{{ npm_name }} nope.txt >/dev/null 2>&1; status=$?; echo "exit status: $status"; test "$status" -eq 1

verify.name: stdin
verify.cmd: set +e; out=$(printf 'alpha beta\ngamma\n' | ./bin/{{ npm_name }} -w); status=$?; echo "stdin: $out"; test "$status" -eq 0; test "$out" = '3'

verify.name: parity
verify.cmd:
mkdir -p .parity; printf 'alpha beta
gamma delta
' > .parity/p1.txt; printf 'alpha beta
gamma' > .parity/p2.txt; printf 'h\303\251llo w\303\266rld
' > .parity/p3.txt; : > .parity/p4.txt; printf 'a	b\vc d
' > .parity/p5.txt; for f in .parity/p*.txt; do ours=$(./bin/{{ npm_name }} -l -w -c "$f"); theirs=$(wc -l -w -c "$f"); test "$ours" = "$theirs" || { echo "$f: $ours"; echo "wc:     $theirs"; exit 1; }; done
